exit.title: Where your traffic comes out
exit.lede: Sites see the exit, not you. A change applies to everyone who uses {{name}}'s proxy.
exit.stopped: Start {{name}} to use its proxy and see where requests leave from.
exit.noAddress: The exit can be set once {{name}} has an address.
exit.unavailable: Exit set: {{proxy}}. {{name}} can't reach it right now. Until it works again or you clear it, requests through the proxy are refused (error 502), never sent from {{name}}'s own address.
exit.unnamed: {{name}} has an exit set that it cannot read. Requests through the proxy are refused (502) until you set another exit or clear it; they are never sent from {{name}}'s own address instead.
exit.setOld: Requests are set to leave through {{proxy}}.
exit.login: Login: set (the Hub never reads it back).
exit.local: This exit seems to run on someone's own machine, started with the hoody command-line tool. If you clear it, {{name}} stops using that machine.
exit.noWrite: You can see the exit, but changing it needs account access.
exit.clear.title: Go back to {{name}}'s own address?
exit.clear.body: Requests through the proxy will leave from {{name}}'s address again.
exit.clear.bodyLogin: Requests through the proxy leave from {{name}}'s address again. The current exit's login is unreadable here: only someone who has it can set it again.
exit.form.title: Use another exit
exit.form.permissions: Set access rules on {{name}}'s proxy first. Its address is the only key to it, so without rules anyone who has the address can send traffic through your exit.
exit.form.refuse: If the proxy you enter cannot be reached, {{name}} refuses requests (502) rather than sending them from its own address.
exit.form.scheme.socks5h: SOCKS5, names resolved by the proxy (socks5h)
exit.form.host.help: A host name or an IPv4 address.
exit.form.host.bad: Enter only a host name or an IPv4 address, without a scheme, port or path.
exit.form.password.help: Sent once to {{name}}; the Hub never keeps it or shows it again.
exit.form.password.needsUser: A password needs a user name.
exit.form.replaceLogin: The current exit has a login the Hub cannot read. Replacing it cannot be undone from here.
exit.form.failed: {{name}} did not accept that proxy. Check the type, host and port. If the host name could not be found, try again in a moment.
exit.held.set: {{name}} may already be set to leave through {{proxy}}. Check again before changing it.
exit.held.setLogin: {{name}} may already be set to leave through {{proxy}}, with your login. The Hub cannot read a login back, so a check cannot confirm it: stop tracking once you know whether it went through.
exit.held.clear: {{name}} may already be back on its own address. Check again before changing it.
exit.held.elsewhere: It was sent from another page or tab; it is settled there.
exit.held.dismissBody: Only stop tracking if you are sure the change did not go through. The setting shown above is what {{name}} reports now.
net.exit.notReported: {{name}} doesn't report whether this exit works.
net.refused: Requests are refused (502) until it works or you clear it. They're never sent from {{name}}'s own address.
net.refused.unnamed: Requests are refused (502) until you set another exit or clear it. They're never sent from {{name}}'s own address.
exit.pick.label: Leave from
exit.form.why: Everything sent through {{name}}'s proxy then leaves from that exit: for scraping, checking a site from another region, or one fixed IP.
exit.pick.own.desc: Sites see the address of {{name}}'s server. Nothing to set up.
exit.pick.computer.desc: Traffic goes through that computer's proxy and leaves from its current exit. With no exit or VPN of its own, that is its server's address: pick one on another server for a different IP.
exit.pick.proxy.desc: A SOCKS5 or HTTP(S) proxy you have, so sites see the IP you chose.
exit.pick.off.desc: Blocks new outgoing connections. The computer stays reachable and the exit chosen here is kept.
exit.pick.off.why: Blocks new outgoing TCP and UDP connections and IPv4 ping; DNS and DHCP with its host stay open. These rules do not block incoming connections or their replies, so terminals, Hoody Kit programs and ports stay reachable; other firewall rules still apply, and a program that needs new outgoing connections can stop working once its open connections end.
exit.pick.off.on: Internet access is blocked for {{name}}. The exit chosen here is kept and applies again when internet access is turned back on (Internet access, above).
exit.off.body: Nothing about the exit changes. Next, Internet access asks before it blocks; allow it again there.
exit.computer.label: Computer
exit.computer.none: None of your other computers can be an exit now: it needs to be running, on a server other than {{name}}'s.
exit.computer.rules: If {{other}}'s proxy has access rules, allow {{name}}'s address there, or its requests are refused.
net.exit.label: Exit
exit.reason.unread: The exit could not be read yet. Wait for it, or check again.
exit.reason.wait: A change of the exit is on its way or waiting. Try again once it is done.
exit.form.need.both: Enter the proxy host and the port to use this exit.
exit.form.need.host: Enter the proxy host to use this exit.
exit.form.need.port: Enter the port to use this exit.
exit.computer.need: Choose the computer to leave through.
